title: Navigation and Listing
subtitle: pwd, ls, cd, tree — moving around the filesystem without a mouse
author: KERNAL Team

content.code:
/               root of the filesystem
├── bin/        essential command binaries (ls, cp, bash)
├── etc/        configuration files
├── home/       user home directories
│   ├── alice/  alice's home: ~
│   └── bob/    bob's home
├── usr/        user programs (most installed software)
│   └── bin/    non-essential binaries (most commands you run)
├── var/        variable data (logs, databases)
│   └── log/    system logs
├── tmp/        temporary files (cleared on reboot)
├── opt/        optional/third-party software
├── proc/       virtual filesystem: running processes info
└── dev/        device files

# Where am I?
pwd          # Print Working Directory → /home/alice/projects

# List directory contents
ls            # basic list
ls -l         # long format: permissions, owner, size, date
ls -la        # include hidden files (dotfiles)
ls -lh        # human-readable sizes (K, M, G)
ls -lt        # sort by modification time (newest first)
ls -lS        # sort by size (largest first)
ls /var/log   # list a specific directory

# Change directory
cd projects          # relative: go into 'projects' in current dir
cd /home/alice       # absolute: go to exact path
cd ~                 # home directory
cd                   # same as cd ~ (no argument = home)
cd ..                # up one level (parent directory)
cd ../..             # up two levels
cd -                 # go back to previous directory

# Quick tip: Tab completes directory names
cd proj<Tab>         # autocompletes to 'projects' if unique

drwxr-xr-x  3  alice  staff   96  Oct  6 10:30  projects/
-rw-r--r--  1  alice  staff  1234  Oct  5 14:22  README.md
-rwxr-xr-x  1  alice  staff  4096  Oct  4 09:15  deploy.sh

│          │  │     │       │     │              └─ filename
│          │  │     │       │     └─ modification date
│          │  │     │       └─ file size in bytes
│          │  │     └─ group owner
│          │  └─ user owner
│          └─ number of hard links
└─ permissions (d=directory, -=file, l=symlink, then rwxrwxrwx)

Permissions breakdown: drwxr-xr-x
  d         = directory
  rwx       = owner can read, write, execute
  r-x       = group can read, execute (not write)
  r-x       = others can read, execute

content.text: ~ is your home directory. It expands to /home/username (Linux) or /Users/username (macOS). Use ~ in paths: cd ~/projects, ls ~/Downloads. . means current directory, .. means parent directory.

questions.question: You are in /home/alice/projects/myapp/src. What does 'cd ../../..' do?
questions.explanation: Each .. goes up one level. Starting from /home/alice/projects/myapp/src: first .. → /home/alice/projects/myapp, second .. → /home/alice/projects, third .. → /home/alice. So cd ../../.. takes you to /home/alice (your home directory).

faq.a: Files and directories whose names start with a dot (.) are hidden by default — ls doesn't show them without -a. Dotfiles are used for configuration: ~/.bashrc (bash config), ~/.gitconfig (git config), ~/.ssh/ (SSH keys). The convention is that dotfiles are config files that shouldn't clutter normal directory listings.

examples: Every Docker Dockerfile starts with WORKDIR /app — setting the working directory, equivalent to cd /app
cd - (go back to previous directory) is invaluable when switching between two directories repeatedly during development
